newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Ramco eyes ex-Soviet Georgia oil projects.
newsitem.headline: Ramco eyes ex-Soviet Georgia oil projects.

text.p: Ramco Energy PLC of Britain plans to form a joint venture with the former Soviet republic of Georgia to develop its oil and gas reserves, a Georgian energy official said on Friday.
Revaz Tevzadze, chairman of state oil organisation Gruzneft, told Reuters that the two sides would form a venture to explore and develop an onshore area known as Block Ten.
"We will probablly sign an agreement on cooperation with Ramco Energy by the end of May", he said, adding that Ramco was ready to invest tens of millions of dollars over 25 years.
"Georgia has very interesting oil structures which have not yet been studied," he said.
Block Ten covers about 1,360 square km in the northeastern Kekhetia region.
Wells drilled in the area have confirmed the existence of light low-sulphur oil there, but there is no comprehensive data yet on volumes.
"Possible oil resources in Georgia are estimated at 560 million tonnes, including 200 million tonnes in the Black Sea shelf," Tevzadze said.
He forecast Georgian crude oil output rising in 1997 to 250,000 tonnes (5,000 barrels per day) from 128,000 tonnes (2,560 bpd) in 1996 and 42,000 (840 bpd) in 1995.
"We believe that within two or three years, Georgia will be capable of meeting its internal demand for oil", he said.
Georgia's peak output, during the early 1980s, was around 3.3 million tonnes a year (66,000 bpd).
